text:
Connor Bedard had shoulder surgery and is out until around late March. He had 18 points in 15 games, and Daily Faceoff summed up the reaction plainly: it "sums up a lost Blackhawks season." The odd part is that Chicago has looked lively since. The Hawks are 3-1-1 in their last five and won 6-3 in Vancouver on Sunday behind Roman Kantserov's hat trick; Kantserov became the first rookie this season to reach ten goals. Frank Nazar has seven goals in a six-game point streak, and his ice time has climbed from about 18 minutes to almost 22.

Our numbers see the bounces in that. Nazar is hot partly on finishing, and for the season Chicago takes 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets), with a -31 goal difference and playoff odds of 0.3%. Still, there's plenty to watch: Sam Rinzel just joined Bobby Orr, Borje Salming and Gordie Howe as the only defensemen with five straight multi-assist games, and Patrick Kane has a five-game point streak. Both our sleepers are Hawks: Ryan Donato at 17% to score from Bedard's old spot, and Nazar at 59% for a point.

Seattle changes goalies. Joey Daccord starts over Philipp Grubauer, and he hasn't found it yet: .877 in eleven games, 3.3 goals worse than his shots deserved. That's one reason Donato makes our list. Spencer Knight, at the other end, is at -1.9 himself, so neither crease has been an advantage this fall.

The Kraken's young story is Berkly Catton, who set a franchise mark with his first NHL hat trick and has nine points in ten, some of it on luck by our numbers. Matty Beniers has goals in three straight and runs the top power play with Jared McCann out until January. Bobby McMann has no goals in 14 games on 2.9 expected. Frederick Gaudreau plays his 500th NHL game. Seattle sits at 35% to make the playoffs.
headline: Daccord gets the call against a Bedard-less Chicago
